instruction: We represent Fatesk Interactive Entertainment, LLC, the video game publisher, as licensee in its software license arrangement with Drupuv Systems, Inc. Before Fatesk commits, it needs a clear picture of where this deal leaves it exposed and what we should push for. Please review the matter folder: fatesk_drupuv_platform_license_agreement.md, nimbus_implementation_statement_of_work.md, fatesk_drupuv_term_sheet.md, nimbus_service_level_schedule.md and fatesk_wilmington_studio_office_lease.md. Use your judgment on how much each one bears on the license deal. Then send me a memo that lists each issue you identify. For each issue, say where it appears (document and section), explain why it matters for Fatesk, and give a recommended fix, such as proposed language or a negotiating position. Put the issues that matter most to the client first. If something is ambiguous or you need facts from the client to resolve it, flag it as an open question rather than assuming. Keep it practical; I'd like to use it to frame our markup and the call with the client.

rubric.text: The response concludes that the SOW's choice of California law and exclusive San Francisco County forum overrides the License Agreement's Delaware law and Wilmington, Delaware forum for implementation disputes, so related claims would be split between two laws and two forums. It identifies the location as the SOW's governing law and venue section (Section 9), explains why this matters to Fatesk, and recommends a fix.
hints: laws of the State of California

rubric.text: The response concludes that the SLA Schedule's narrow 'Severity 1 Incident' definition (complete unavailability to all End Users in all regions) controls over the License Agreement's definition (unavailability to 10% or more of End Users), undermining the License Agreement's Severity 1 protections. It identifies the location as the Service Level Schedule Section 2.1, explains why this matters to Fatesk, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Drupuv can assign the License Agreement without Fatesk's consent to any person, including a Fatesk competitor, contrary to the term sheet. It identifies the location as License Agreement Section 15.2 and/or the 'Permitted Transfer' definition in Section 1, explains why this matters to Fatesk, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the License Agreement automatically renews for successive three-year terms unless notice of non-renewal is given within a 30-day window between 150 and 120 days before term end, departing from the term sheet's one-year renewals with 90 days' notice. It identifies the location as License Agreement Section 12.2, explains why this matters to Fatesk, and recommends a fix.

The response states that the License Agreement's order-of-precedence clause (Section 17.4) gives the SOW and/or the SLA Schedule priority over the License Agreement within their respective subject areas.
The response states that the annual license fee is $1,840,000 per contract year.
The response is a memo addressed to the supervising partner that, for each issue, gives the document and section where it appears, why it matters for Fatesk, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that the License Agreement's Delaware governing law and Wilmington forum govern disputes over Implementation Services under the SOW.
The response claims that the License Agreement renews for one-year renewal terms.
